fi-chromobotia-macracanthus.title: Clown Loach
fi-chromobotia-macracanthus.summary: A playful, social loach that's sold small but grows big and lives a long time. It needs a group and a very large tank.
rows: Up to about 12 in (30 cm). Seriously Fish lists up to 16 in. Grows slowly
72 × 24 in footprint (about 170 gal) minimum for an adult group. Juveniles can grow on in smaller tanks with frequent water changes
Peaceful but boisterous. It can intimidate small fish and nip long fins
Keep at least 5–6, ideally 10+. Kept alone or in pairs they can turn withdrawn or aggressive
Mostly carnivore. Quality sinking foods, frozen bloodworm and brine shrimp, plus vegetables like cucumber, melon or blanched spinach. Eats snails but isn't a reliable snail cure
Moderate. Needs a mature tank, spotless water and 30–50% weekly water changes
notes: Give it lots of hiding spots, smooth rocks and driftwood, and avoid sharp decor.
Use a tight lid because they jump. They may eat soft-leaved plants.
A well-kept clown loach can live more than 20 years.
warn: Needs a very large tank as an adult.
Not for new or immature tanks.

fi-botia-almorhae.title: Yo-Yo Loach
fi-botia-almorhae.summary: The yo-yo loach, Botia almorhae, is a botiid loach from parts of the Ganges River drainage in northern India and possibly Nepal. It is often called the 'Pakistani' loach, but that name is a misnomer.…
rows: Pairs or small groups depending on setup
notes: All botiids need a well-structured set-up although the actual choice of décor is more-or-less down to personal taste.
A natural-style arrangement could include a substrate of sand or fine gravel with lots of smooth, water-worn rocks and pebbles plus driftwood roots and branches.

fi-lepidocephalichthys-berdmorei.title: Berdmore's Loach
fi-lepidocephalichthys-berdmorei.summary: Lepidocephalichthys berdmorei is a cobitid loach found across Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, north-eastern India and Bangladesh. One of the most frequently-traded members of the genus, it is an excellent…
rows: Carnivore / micropredator. Probably a micropredator feeding on insect larvae and suchlike in nature.
Thought to have been described from the Sittaung River basin, Bago Division, Myanmar but currently accepted to have a wide distribution including the following river systems and…
notes: This species will do well in most well-maintained aquaria if plenty of hiding places are provided and should not harm softer-leaved plants.
However we highly recommend keeping it in a set-up designed to resemble a flowing stream with a substrate of variably-sized rocks, gravel and some water-worn boulders.

fi-pangio-kuhlii.title: Kuhlii Loach
fi-pangio-kuhlii.summary: Usually sold as the 'kuhli' loach, Pangio semicincta is a cobitid loach from Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra and Borneo. It lives in shallow forest streams and swamps, often in black water, and is…
rows: group of at least 5-6 specimens should be the minimum purchased.

Carnivore / micropredator. Chiefly a micropredator sifting mouthfuls of substrate through the mouth and gills from which insect larvae, small crustaceans and suchlike are extracted with a proportion of the natural diet also…
Currently accepted to occur in Peninsular Malaysia plus the Great Sunda Islands of Sumatra and Borneo but the true extent of its distribution is unclear.
notes: Use a soft, sandy substrate since this species likes to dig and tends to spend some of its time completely buried.
When coarser gravel is used it may become stressed or damage itself, and feeding behaviour can be inhibited.

fi-misgurnus-anguillicaudatus.title: Misgurnus anguillicaudatus
fi-misgurnus-anguillicaudatus.summary: The oriental weather loach, Misgurnus anguillicaudatus, is a loach native to Siberia, Korea, Japan, China and northern Vietnam. Known in the United States as the 'dojo loach', it is one of the most…
rows: Carnivore / micropredator. Chiefly a predator foraging for insect larvae, small crustaceans and suchlike.
Native to Siberia, Sakhalin island, Korea, Japan, China, northern Vietnam and possibly Laos (it remains unknown whether the species is native or was introduced there) but alien…
notes: Not difficult to keep but must be provided with a soft, sandy or fine gravel substrate since some of its time is spent completely buried, or with only eyes protruding.
When coarser material is used it may become stressed or damage itself trying to dig, and feeding behaviour can be inhibited.
